EXAM: PET/CT SKULL BASE TO MID-THIGH
INDICATION: Restaging of lymphoma.
COMPARISON: PET/CT from 3 months earlier.

Findings:
No hypermetabolic lymphadenopathy in the neck, chest, abdomen, or
pelvis.
Lungs: 3.8 mm solid nodule in the right upper lobe.
Heart size is normal. No pericardial effusion.

IMPRESSION:
1. Complete metabolic response. No FDG-avid disease.
2. Small incidental pulmonary nodule under 6 mm. Per Fleischner
Society guidelines, no routine follow-up is required; optional CT in
12 months if high risk.

EXAM: LDCT LUNG CANCER SCREENING
CLINICAL HISTORY: Lung cancer screening. Baseline exam.
TECHNIQUE: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without intravenous
contrast.
COMPARISON: None.

FINDINGS:
Lungs: 24.9 mm solid nodule with spiculated margins in the right lower
lobe (series 5, image 177).
Mild centrilobular emphysema, upper lobe predominant.
Heart size is normal. No pericardial effusion.

Impression:
1. Spiculated solid pulmonary nodule, highly suspicious for
malignancy.
Lung RADS 4X
RECOMMENDATION: Diagnostic chest CT with or without contrast, PET/CT
and/or tissue sampling. Referral to pulmonology or thoracic surgery is
recommended.
